newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea says will respond to U.N. food appeal.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea says will respond to U.N. food appeal.

text.p: South Korea is ready to respond to a World Food Programme appeal for $41.6 million in new food aid for North Korea, a senior Seoul official said on Thursday.

"We haven't been officially notified yet but our position is that we will participate and we will do our share," the official with the National Unification Ministry, who declined to be named, said by telephone.

The U.N.'s food aid agency said on Wednesday it had launched an urgent appeal to raise 100,000 metric tonnes of aid for North Korea, where it said people were receiving a quarter of their minimum daily food needs.

But the appeal has now been complicated by a drama between the two Koreas over the fate of a top Pyongyang official who Seoul says is seeking asylum at its Beijing embassy and North Korea insists may have been kidnapped.

"North Korea's attitude is the most important thing. There is a possibility that North Korea will counter strongly. We are examining the situation attentively," the official said, referring to the defection wrangle.
Food aid has often been held hostage to political crises between the communist North and the capitalist South.
